uncited: It addresses the problem of converging to geometrically accurate and photometrically correct scene representations from sparse or noisy input data.
**Ray Casting and Sampling:** For each training image, cast a ray $\mathbf{r}$ through each pixel.
Underflow or overflow can occur if densities are not properly bounded or if step sizes $\delta_i$ are extremely small/large [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].

*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot M \cdot K)$ per iteration, where $N$ is the number of pixels, $M$ is the number of rays per pixel (if multi-sample), and $K$ is the number of samples per ray [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot K)$ to store intermediate transmittance and density values for backpropagation if using reverse-mode AD [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].
Adjoint methods or analytic inversion can reduce this to $O(N)$ [44-radiance-field-optimization.md].

*   **When Not to Use:** When geometric accuracy is paramount and surface-based representations are preferred (use Eikonal regularization instead) [3430-neural-surface-rendering-training-eikonal-boundary-regulariz.md]; when global consistency is required over local optimization [5436-global-optimization.md].
